checks: Read 2adcc478e651c9c4 §§3–4, (5)–(9). At the middle integer base the endpoint weights in any lift combination are equal. Their joint contribution is a scaled point of (A+B)/2, so all three integer fibers are actual. Independence of the d retained normals gives u≠0.

The undeformed cap contains all of A by the separator premise and only a hyperplane-null trace on B by B⊆T. Tilting to coefficient 1−ε keeps the exact K trace, loses the strict layer of A, and gains exactly B_ε. It continues to contain (0,0), so subtracting the true raw depth gives Δ≥L_A−|B_ε| for every ε≥0.

The inner simplex has r+1 affinely independent face vertices and p=d−r positive-height interior vertices. Its p-coordinate marginal is d!/r! times (1−s)^r. For s≤ε/H_*≤1/2 this is at least d!/(r!2^r). Multiplying by the small coordinate simplex volume gives the stated L exactly.

The assumption r>d−k implies 1≤p<k. At the stated ε_* the upper cap term is at most half the layer lower bound. In the facet case r=d−1 implies k≥2 under the same assumption, and integrating the actual cone section with coarea 1/||u|| gives the stated L_f. Both lower bounds are strictly positive.
If Δ=0, the finite inequality applies for all nonnegative ε and rules out any face at height −1 of dimension greater than d−k.

dependencies.hypotheses: Same-batch input has the identical enclosing simplex T, B⊆T, the same probability weights with one omitted index, nonzero u and support size k. Its bound is exactly |B_ε|≤Cε^k with the constant used here. Admission depends on the predecessor's independent approval.

overlap.comparison: Uses genuine finite base tilts at a fixed mark to equalize endpoint cap masses starting from a critical cap. This draft allows a noncritical initial averaged cap and quantifies its slack from the differing endpoint decay orders.
Provides a strict separator in its bad-source critical circuit setting. It does not make the new cap critical or prove a positive-slack estimate from its face dimension.

readability: The facet formula remains inside the hypothesis r>d−k; this is why its exponent 1/(k−1) is well-defined. An explicit reminder in the statement would reduce rereading.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The fixed-source tilt gives an exact slack inequality, and the inner simplex and facet cone prove the stated positive lower bounds under the face-dimension hypothesis.
